title: In Vitro Multi-Omic Predictive Markers of Treatment Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using a Tumoroid Biobank
official: In Vitro Investigation of Multi-Omic Predictive Markers for Sensitivity and Resistance to Standard Treatments in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through the Generation of a Tumoroid Biobank
summary:
HCCspoTARGET is a prospective study in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The study aims to establish patient-derived tumor organoid models from tumor samples collected during routine clinical care. These organoids will be used to better understand tumor biology and to evaluate potential treatment responses in a laboratory setting.

The study will also collect clinical, pathological, and molecular data to investigate associations between organoid characteristics and patient outcomes. The long-term goal is to support the development of personalized treatment strategies for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.

interventions.name: Tumor Sample Collection and Organoid Generation

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male or female patients aged 18 years or older.
* Patient who has provided written informed consent.
* Patient with suspected hepatocellular carcinoma, metastatic or non-metastatic, or recurrent disease, for whom a diagnostic biopsy or tumor resection surgery has been planned.
* Patient affiliated with, or beneficiary of, a health insurance system.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient who underwent emergency liver cancer surgery.
* Patient in an emergency situation or unable to provide informed consent. Adults under legal protection (guardianship, trusteeship, or judicial protection).
* Patient unable to comply with study follow-up procedures for geographical, social, or psychological reasons.
* Patient with another active cancer or a previously treated cancer for which the last treatment was administered less than 3 years before inclusion.
* Pregnant women or women who may become pregnant and are not using effective contraception.

Study-Specific Exclusion After Enrollment:

Patients will be excluded from the study if the biopsy does not confirm the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
